issues.title: Phase 1 assay confounds: free-form JSON failure and candidate-label leakage
issues.body:
## Findings
Two assay-level confounds were found while running the real sandbox SmolLM2-135M model.

### 1. Output-format confound
The 135M model can run inference correctly, but free-form JSON generation repeatedly produces malformed/repetitive JSON. Scoring those failures as selection/control failures conflates semantic decision quality with serialization/instruction-following capacity.

### 2. Candidate-label leakage
The current sandbox S2 builder uses claim text such as `Domain-rule-compatible transition` for expected-valid candidates and `Plausible but rule-incompatible transition` for the invalid candidate. These strings reveal the oracle label and make candidate selection scientifically invalid.

## Resolution
Use a factorized categorical assay with llama.cpp grammar-constrained outputs:
- candidate admissibility: `YES | NO`, one candidate at a time;
- reframing: `YES | NO`;
- closure: `CLOSE | CONTINUE`.

Candidate payloads must contain only task facts, explicit domain rules, operation semantics, dependencies/evidence, and relation type. They must not contain `valid`, `invalid`, `compatible`, `incompatible`, oracle IDs, or expected outcomes.

## Acceptance criteria
- All outputs are parseable by construction.
- No oracle-validity adjectives appear in candidate payloads.
- Same semantic information is presented to EC and LLM arms.
- Selection, reframe, and closure are scored separately.
- Free-form JSON result is retained only as an instruction-following diagnostic, not the primary architecture comparison.

GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: Phase 1 capacity sweep: repeat control-mirror assay with ~0.5B lightweight model
issues.body:

Per `PHASE1_MVP_TCC_V1`, run exactly one ~1.5B capacity branch with the same assay before making an architecture-level LLM conclusion. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M is the target unless infrastructure blocks it. No prompt/fixture/threshold change is authorized.

GitHub Actions remain disabled. Google Drive is not used.

issues.title: Ingress writer gap: external model fetch to GitHub text shards without Drive persistence
issues.body:
## Finding
GitHub connector UTF-8 text-shard transport is now verified end-to-end for a deterministic payload, but the source-side writer for a real ~0.5B GGUF is not yet connector-native.

## Verified
- GitHub connector reads Base64 shards reliably.
- Returned Git blob SHA matches the locally calculated Git blob SHA.
- Base64 decode reproduces the source binary SHA exactly.
- Direct HF/Xet binary download is still blocked at the sandbox safe-open boundary.

## Current external fetch runner
The existing `OBSCURA_GAS_RELAY` / Apps Script range fetcher can fetch public binary ranges and Base64-encode them, but its UrlFetch daily quota is currently exhausted (`Service invoked too many times for one day: urlfetch`).

## Design target
`external fetcher -> Base64 shards -> GitHub repo -> GitHub connector -> sandbox`

Google Drive must not be used as persistent model storage. If Google Sheets is temporarily required as an execution surface, each temporary range must be removed after GitHub/sandbox verification.

## Acceptance criteria
- Fetch a real Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct GGUF source range outside sandbox.
- Write it to GitHub as verified Base64 text shard(s) without persisting the model in Drive.
- Reconstruct in sandbox with per-shard and final SHA verification.
- Complete llama.cpp smoke inference.
- Delete transient staging.
- GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: Product attachment blocker: connect Generic Binary Ingress MCP to ChatGPT from current plan
issues.body:
## Status
Server-side ingress is complete and qualified. Issue #15 is closed.

## Verified server qualification
- Render-hosted HTTPS MCP live.
- Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf full fetch PASS: 397,808,192 bytes.
- SHA-256 exact match: `6eb923e7d26e9cea28811e1a8e852009b21242fb157b26149d3b188f3a8c8653`.
- OAuth 2.1 Protected Resource Metadata PASS.
- Authorization Server Metadata PASS.
- Dynamic Client Registration PASS.
- PKCE S256 authorization code PASS.
- RFC 9207 issuer identification PASS.
- `offline_access` / refresh token PASS.
- Bearer-authenticated MCP initialize PASS.
- tools/list PASS.
- artifact_fetch tool PASS.
- artifact_delete tool PASS.

## Remaining blocker
Attach this remote MCP to ChatGPT as a custom app/plugin from the user's current account.

Current OpenAI documentation (checked 2026-10-01) lists custom MCP developer mode for Business and Enterprise/Edu. Pro can connect read/fetch MCPs in developer mode. Plus is not listed for custom MCP developer mode. The current account is Plus, so this appears to be a product/plan boundary rather than an MCP implementation defect.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Establish a supported ChatGPT attachment path for the current account OR document the exact plan/product requirement.
2. ChatGPT performs OAuth linking to `https://generic-binary-ingress-mcp.onrender.com/mcp`.
3. ChatGPT scans and sees artifact tools.
4. Invoke `artifact_fetch` from ChatGPT.
5. Materialize/read artifact chunks into sandbox and reconstruct the 0.5B GGUF.
6. Run llama.cpp inference and resume Phase 1 135M vs 0.5B comparison.

## Non-goals
- Do not return to Drive persistence.
- Do not use Mac/Remote Desktop unless no supported cloud/connector path exists.
- Do not change the frozen Phase 1 fixture/grammar/control-rule comparison conditions.

issues.title: Site bridge: expose Render Generic Binary Ingress through ChatGPT Sites plugin
issues.body:
## Goal
Create a ChatGPT Site-hosted MCP app/plugin that exposes the already-qualified Render Generic Binary Ingress MCP to a Plus account without relying on custom-MCP Developer Mode.

## Architecture
ChatGPT plugin -> Site-hosted MCP tools -> Render Generic Binary Ingress MCP -> external binary source.

## Constraints
- Do not duplicate artifact storage in the Site.
- Do not move model/inference logic into the Site.
- Proxy only the four artifact operations: fetch, info, bounded chunk read/link, delete.
- Keep the Render OAuth server as the authority for the upstream MCP.
- No Drive persistence, no Mac/Remote Desktop, no GitHub Actions.
- Preserve SHA/size fail-closed semantics.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Site can make outbound HTTPS calls to the Render MCP endpoint.
2. Site bridge can complete OAuth/DCR/PKCE to Render or use an equivalent secure server-side credential flow supported by Sites.
3. Site-hosted tools expose artifact_fetch/info/chunk/delete with schemas equivalent to the Render MCP.
4. Publishing the Site creates a personal plugin visible on the Plus account.
5. Plugin tool invocation reaches Render and returns the verified artifact manifest.
6. A bounded chunk can be retrieved through the plugin without embedding the entire artifact in one response.
7. 0.5B GGUF can be reconstructed in sandbox and SHA-verified.
8. Phase 1 135M vs 0.5B comparison resumes unchanged.

## Known upstream qualification
Render MCP E2E already passes OAuth metadata, DCR, PKCE, refresh, MCP initialize, tools/list, artifact_fetch and artifact_delete. Full Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4_K_M fetch also passed at 397,808,192 bytes with expected SHA-256.

issues.title: Site bridge implementation contract and one-shot @Sites build prompt
issues.body:
## One-shot Site build prompt
Use this verbatim in ChatGPT Work with @Sites:

> Build a private ChatGPT Site named `Generic Binary Ingress Bridge`. Add an MCP server to the Site with exactly four read/fetch/delete tools that proxy an existing upstream MCP at `https://generic-binary-ingress-mcp.onrender.com/mcp`: `artifact_fetch`, `artifact_info`, `artifact_chunk_link`, and `artifact_delete`. Do not store model binaries persistently in the Site. Preserve upstream input schemas, SHA-256/size fail-closed semantics, 4 MiB bounded chunks, TTL behavior, and SSRF protections. Keep upstream authentication server-side; use OAuth 2.1/DCR/PKCE against the upstream Render service when supported by the Sites runtime, otherwise use a Site secret for a server-side API key fallback. Never expose the secret to client-side code or tool output. Add a `bridge_health` tool that verifies upstream OAuth metadata and MCP initialize without downloading an artifact. Add structured logging for upstream HTTP status, MCP method, latency, and artifact id only; never log authorization headers, tokens, signed URL query strings, or binary contents. Publish the Site privately so ChatGPT creates its associated plugin. Then run: bridge_health -> artifact_fetch of the Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M GGUF with expected SHA-256 `6eb923e7d26e9cea28811e1a8e852009b21242fb157b26149d3b188f3a8c8653` -> artifact_info -> one bounded chunk -> artifact_delete. Report only PASS/FAIL, artifact size/hash, and any blocker.

## Tool contracts
### artifact_fetch
Inputs: `url`, optional `expected_sha256`, `expected_size`, `ttl_seconds`, `max_bytes`.
Output: upstream manifest/resource link; no binary embedding.

### artifact_info
Input: `id` UUID.
Output: manifest only.

### artifact_chunk_link
Inputs: `id`, `offset`, optional `length <= 4194304`.
Output: one bounded resource/chunk reference or bounded blob, never entire artifact.

### artifact_delete
Input: `id` UUID.
Output: `{id, deleted:true}`.

### bridge_health
No input.
Checks: protected resource metadata, authorization server metadata, DCR/PKCE availability, MCP initialize, tools/list. No artifact download.

## Security requirements
- Server-side secrets only.
- No arbitrary client-provided auth headers.
- No raw proxy endpoint.
- No Drive persistence.
- No browser/local-machine dependency.
- No GitHub Actions.
- Redact URL query strings from logs.

## Acceptance
1. Site publishes and creates personal plugin.
2. Plugin connects on Plus account.
3. bridge_health PASS.
4. 397,808,192-byte Qwen GGUF manifest with expected SHA PASS.
5. bounded chunk retrieval PASS.
6. delete PASS.
7. plugin usable from normal chat surface.
